title: TBO Tek’s Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 81% to Rs 926 Cr; profit grows 32%
summary:
Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported an 81.2% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue for the first quarter of FY27, while its profit increased 31.7% during the same period.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 926 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 511 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


 
Hotel and package bookings remained TBO Tek’s largest revenue stream, contributing Rs 800 crore in Q1 FY27, up 89.1% from Rs 423 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from air ticketing increased marginally to Rs 81 crore from Rs 78 crore, while other operating revenue climbed to Rs 45 crore from Rs 10.4 crore.
Including Rs 13 crore in other income, the company’s total income stood at Rs 939 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 524 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a sequential basis, operating revenue grew 13.8% from Rs 814 crore in Q4 FY26.
On the expense front, service fees remained the largest cost component, rising to Rs 373 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 179 crore, while depreciation and finance costs stood at Rs 33 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively.
Overall expenditure grew 83.1% to Rs 835 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 456 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite higher expenses, TBO Tek’s profit increased to Rs 83 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 63 crore in Q1 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit rose 38.3% from Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26.
TBO Tek’s share price closed at Rs 1,522.60, with a total market capitalization of Rs 16,385 crore.

Online trucking platform BlackBuck has released its financial results for the first quarter of FY27 today. The Bengaluru-based company reported a 42% year-on-year growth in its operating scale during the quarter, while its profit increased 24% to Rs 42 crore.
Blackbuck's revenue from operations grew to Rs 204 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 144 crore in Q1 FY26, its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.

Revenue from truck operator services remained BlackBuck's primary source of income, contributing 98.5% of its operating revenue of Rs 201 crore in Q1 FY27. On a quarterly basis, Blackbuck’s operating revenue increased over 10% compared to Rs 185 crore in Q4 FY26.
Employee benefit expenses accounted for over 24% of BlackBuck's total expenditure and increased 16% year-on-year to Rs 43 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 37 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.
Depreciation and other operating expenses pushed BlackBuck's total expenditure to Rs 178 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 114 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.
BlackBuck reported a 24% year-on-year growth in profit to Rs 42 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 34 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, however, the company's profit declined 36% from Rs 66 crore in Q4 FY26.

title: Exclusive: OfBusiness reports consolidated profit of Rs 724 Cr on Rs 20,645 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
IPO-bound B2B commerce and financing platform OfBusiness reported a 21% year-on-year growth in its profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 724 crore in FY26 from Rs 597 crore in the previous fiscal, while its consolidated revenue stood at Rs 20,645 crore.
The company's commerce business, which spans metals, chemicals, apparel and food processing, recorded a revenue of Rs 19,174 crore during the fiscal year. Its EBITDA grew 34% to Rs 769 crore in FY26 from Rs 575 crore in FY25, while EBITDA margin expanded to 4% from 2.6% a year ago.
OfBusiness also reported a sharp improvement in cash generation, with operating cash flow from its commerce business rising to Rs 1,302 crore in FY26 from Rs 715 crore in the previous fiscal. The company turned free cash flow to firm (FCFF) positive for the first time, reporting Rs 390 crore during the year.
Its financing arm, Oxyzo Financial Services, reported an asset base of Rs 11,800 crore in FY26, 28% higher than the previous fiscal. The lending business posted a return on assets of 3.8% and maintained a gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio of 0.75%.
Founded in 2015 by Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra, Bhuvan Gupta and Vasant Sridhar, OfBusiness operates a technology-led platform that offers SMEs raw material procurement, working capital financing, and tender intelligence solutions. 
Its tender intelligence platform, BidAssist, has crossed 1.5 million business users and aggregates over 50,000 live tenders daily from authorities and portals across India. The platform uses AI to match tenders with business profiles, helps users track win rates and competitors in live bids, and serves as a customer acquisition channel for OfBusiness's commerce and financing businesses.
The company's workforce has also crossed 30,000 employees, nearly doubling over the past year, led by the expansion of its apparel business in South India.
Commenting on the performance, co-founder and CEO Asish Mohapatra said, “The year saw the Group crossing significant milestones, becoming free cash flow to firm positive in the Commerce business and crossing the Rs 10,000 crore AuM mark in lending. FY27 will be a pivotal year for us as returns from prior investments play out.”

title: CarTrade reports Rs 201 Cr revenue and Rs 57 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
summary:
Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade announced its financial results for the first quarter of FY27 on Wednesday, reporting over 16% year-on-year growth in its revenue from operations. The company's profit also increased 21% to Rs 57 crore during the quarter.
CarTrade’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 201 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 173 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Mumbai-based company operates across three key segments: Consumer, Remarketing, and Classifieds. The Consumer segment remained the largest contributor, with Rs 78 crore in revenue during Q1 FY27, followed by Remarketing at Rs 67 crore and Classifieds at Rs 62 crore, before Rs 6.4 crore in intersegment eliminations.

As part of its expansion strategy, the company plans to increase its retail footprint to 350 stores by FY28 from around 280 currently. While the brand will continue opening company-owned stores in metro cities, it plans to adopt a franchise-led model in smaller towns.
FNP has raised around $27 million in funding to date, with Lighthouse among its key investors. Yaanendriya, a Bengaluru-based deep tech company building indigenous sensor, navigation, and control technologies for mobile robots and critical applications, has raised Rs 15 crore in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen research and development, accelerate product development, and expand its portfolio of high precision navigation systems for mission critical environments, Yaanendriya said in a press release.
Co-founded in February last year by Vamshi Bharadwaj M V, Vyshak Y, Vijay HP, and Aravind Thumbur, Yaanendriya develops indigenous sensor, navigation, and control technologies for robotics, aerospace, and other critical applications.
Its portfolio includes the SynCore series of navigation controllers for autonomous robotic platforms and the YDX series of high precision inertial sensors deployed across commercial applications globally. The company is also developing navigation systems and a hardware agnostic platform for space and other critical missions, along with high precision MEMS inertial sensors for the NewSpace sector.
Yaanendriya builds sensor and control platforms that enable autonomous systems, including drones, ground robots, spacecraft, and underwater vehicles, to sense motion, estimate their state, and maintain control in environments where GNSS is unavailable, unreliable, or intentionally disrupted.
Its SynCore navigation controllers combine inputs from multiple sensors to estimate orientation, position, and velocity while supporting real time stabilization and control. The platform is deployed by robotics companies across aerial, ground, and underwater applications in sectors such as defence, surveillance, and agriculture.
The company's YDX series of high precision inertial sensors is deployed across four continents in applications including motion capture for gaming, unmanned vehicles, and surgical robots.

title: Pine Labs reports  Rs 737 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps over 4X
summary:
Pine Labs reports  Rs 737 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps over 4X  
Fintech major Pine Labs has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 20% year-on-year growth in operating scale, while its profits jumped 4X to Rs 20 crore during the period.
Pine Labs’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 737 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 616 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Revenue from its digital infrastructure and transaction platform was the largest contributor, which grew 14.9% to Rs 499.12 crore in Q1 FY27. Its issuing and acquiring platform grew by 31% to Rs 237.8 crore during the same period.
The company added Rs 29 crore from non-operating activities, taking its total income to Rs 766 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 653 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a sequential basis, the Bengaluru-based firm’s revenue increased marginally by 5% compared to Rs 701 crore in Q4 FY26.
Employee benefits remained the largest cost centre for Pine Labs, accounting for 36.8% of its overall expenditure. Interestingly, this cost declined 7.9% to Rs 268 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 291 crore in Q1 FY26.
The cost of materials consumed increased 39% to Rs 107 crore, while transaction and related costs surged 61.7% to Rs 97 crore. Depreciation rose 12.3% to Rs 73 crore, whereas other expenses increased 10.9% to Rs 183 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenditure increased 10.6% to Rs 728 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 658 crore in Q1 FY26.
The faster growth in revenue compared to expenses helped Pine Labs to zoom its profit by fourfold to Rs 20 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 5 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a unit level, Pine Labs spent Rs 0.99 to earn a rupee of operating revenue during Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 1.07 in the year-ago quarter.
At 3:05 PM, Pine Labs’ shares were trading at Rs 151 apiece, taking its market capitalization to Rs 17,188 crore.

summary:
The acquisition of edtech platform Unacademy by upGrad has entered its final phase, with the transaction expected to close within the next three weeks, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Sources said that almost all institutional investors have signed the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA), while all angel investors have signed the Share Purchase Agreement (SPA), which leaves only the final formalities before the deal is completed.
According to sources, the all-stock transaction has been pegged at around Rs 1,955 crore. The current deal is slightly lower than the valuation discussed when the deal was announced earlier this year.

In another key development, Unacademy's existing investors will receive one board seat in upGrad after the transaction is completed, according to sources.

title: BigBasket's B2C arm losses cross Rs 3,000 Cr in FY26
summary:
The battle for India's online grocery market has become more intense as platforms chase scale, speed, and profitability. While demand remains strong, profitability continues to remain elusive for most players. Against this backdrop, BigBasket posted marginal growth in FY26 with its operating revenue crossing Rs 8,000 crore, even as its core B2C business continued to bleed. The Tata Digital-backed firm's performance mirrors broader sector trends, where grocery delivery platforms continue to post heavy losses despite rapid expansion.
According to Tata Sons' FY26 annual report, Innovative Retail Concepts, which operates BigBasket's consumer-facing business, recorded a 7.7% increase in turnover to Rs 8,223 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,634 crore in the previous fiscal year. However, its losses widened 66% to Rs 3,073 crore from Rs 1,850 crore during the same period.

BigBasket's losses have risen sharply since its complete pivot to quick commerce in August 2024. The shift has raised operating costs as the company spends more on logistics, dark stores, discounts, and customer retention to compete in the rapidly expanding segment.
Meanwhile, BigBasket's B2B arm, Supermarket Grocery Supplies, which handles procurement and backend operations, reported flat revenue of Rs 2,298 crore in FY26, while its losses remained unchanged at Rs 102 crore during the fiscal year.
Together, the two entities reported Rs 10,521 crore in revenue in FY26, compared to Rs 9,861 crore in the previous fiscal year. Their combined losses stood at Rs 3,175 crore during the year.
Tata Digital, which acquired a majority stake in BigBasket in 2021, remains its largest shareholder with an 84.23% stake.
BigBasket's rival Zepto reported Rs 22,624 crore in revenue and a loss of Rs 5,905 crore in FY26, while quick commerce leader Blinkit posted Rs 15,664 crore in revenue and a positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 102 crore in Q1 FY27.
At the group level, Tata Digital reported a 12% increase in revenue to Rs 35,990 crore in FY26 from Rs 32,188 crore in FY25. However, its net loss widened to Rs 4,974 crore from Rs 4,610 crore during the same period. The company's gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at Rs 46,515 crore in FY26.

The company’s revenue came from two entities: Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions Private Limited, which contributed Rs 2,440 crore, and Tata 1mg Technologies Private Limited, which added Rs 496 crore. Together, the two entities generated Rs 2,936 crore in revenue during FY26.
On the bottom line, Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions reported a loss of Rs 310 crore, while Tata 1mg Technologies remained profitable with a net profit of Rs 23 crore. On a combined basis, Tata 1mg posted a net loss of Rs 287 crore in FY26.
On the balance sheet, the combined Tata 1mg entities had total assets of Rs 2,268 crore at the end of FY26. Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions accounted for Rs 805 crore, while Tata 1mg Technologies held assets worth Rs 1,463 crore.
Their combined liabilities stood at Rs 1,601 crore, including Rs 1,509 crore for Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions and Rs 92 crore for Tata 1mg Technologies.
The combined entities reported a negative reserves and surplus balance of Rs 167 crore. While Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions had a negative reserves and surplus balance of Rs 1,538 crore, Tata 1mg Technologies reported a positive reserves and surplus of Rs 1,371 crore.
In the online healthcare space, Tata 1mg competes with Reliance-backed Netmeds, PharmEasy, and Apollo 24/7.
Tata Digital acquired a majority stake in 1mg in June 2021 as part of its strategy to build a digital ecosystem spanning grocery, electronics, healthcare, financial services, and payments.

title: Delhi HC halts Unity SFB’s share capital plan in BharatPe dispute
summary:
The Delhi High Court has restrained Unity Small Finance Bank (Unity SFB) from moving ahead with a proposal to increase its authorised share capital, giving interim relief to BharatPe in an ongoing shareholder dispute between the two stakeholders.
According to court proceedings, the bank had proposed increasing its authorised share capital from Rs 4,000 crore to Rs 4,900 crore. The proposal was aimed at facilitating the conversion of certain warrants into compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) before their expiry later this year.
BharatPe opposed the move and argued that the proposal could not be carried out without its consent under the shareholders' agreement. The fintech company also claimed that the conversion would significantly dilute its stake in Unity SFB.
The High Court has directed the bank not to place the proposal before its board for now, while the dispute is being resolved through arbitration. The order is interim in nature and does not decide the merits of the case.
The dispute marks the latest chapter in the evolving relationship between BharatPe and Centrum Group, the two key shareholders of Unity SFB.
Unity Small Finance Bank was launched in 2021 after a consortium led by BharatPe and Centrum Financial Services took over the troubled Punjab and Maharashtra Cooperative (PMC) Bank under a Reserve Bank of India-backed reconstruction scheme. BharatPe initially emerged as one of the largest shareholders in the bank, with a stake close to 49%.
However, differences have surfaced between the shareholders over governance and capital-related decisions. BharatPe has alleged that the proposed capital restructuring would materially reduce its ownership without the approvals required under the shareholder agreement.
The case is significant as it highlights the importance of shareholder rights and governance in financial institutions, particularly those created under regulatory reconstruction plans. The arbitration proceedings will now determine whether the proposed capital increase and share conversion comply with the agreements signed between the parties.

Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd., the parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, reported a 2.4X year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026. The company also posted its first-ever positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 2 crore, led by strong sales growth during the fiscal year.
Bombay Shaving Company’s revenue from operations surged 139% to Rs 635 crore in FY26 from Rs 266 crore in FY25, its consolidated financial report sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) shows.

Visage Lines operates three businesses: Bombay Shaving Company, its flagship men's grooming brand; Bombae, focused on women's personal care; and 100Days, which provides digital commerce and e-commerce growth solutions for consumer brands.
The sale of men's and women's personal care products through Bombay Shaving Company and Bombae accounted for over 91% of the operating revenue at Rs 581 crore in FY26 from Rs 241 crore in FY25. 
Meanwhile, revenue from sale of services doubled to Rs 48 crore in FY26. The company made an additional Rs 6 crore from interest income, which pushed its total revenue to Rs 641 crore in FY25.
In line with its sales growth, the cost of materials consumed was the largest overhead, which grew 2.8X to Rs 370 crore in FY26. title: CBDT issues operational clarity on crypto reporting, exchanges to collect tax residency details
summary:
The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued a detailed guidance note clarifying how crypto exchanges and other virtual digital asset (VDA) service providers should comply with India's new crypto reporting framework under the Income-tax Rules, 2026.
The guidance provides operational clarity on the recently introduced reporting requirements and aligns India's framework with the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).
Under the new framework, crypto exchanges and other Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Providers (RCASPs) will be required to collect additional information from users, including their tax residency status and Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), wherever applicable. The entities will also have to maintain detailed transaction records and submit annual reports to the Income Tax Department.
The guidance further explains how exchanges should identify reportable users, determine the account holder in different scenarios, and handle cross-border transactions where more than one jurisdiction may have reporting obligations. It also distinguishes between crypto-assets, central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), and specified electronic money products for reporting purposes.
The clarification is expected to help crypto exchanges prepare their compliance systems before the reporting rules come into effect. Market participants will need to strengthen their KYC and record-keeping processes to meet the new requirements.
While the guidance does not introduce any new tax on virtual digital assets, it lays down the operational framework for reporting crypto transactions and sharing information with tax authorities.
For India's crypto industry, the latest guidance marks another step towards a more regulated environment. Exchanges will now need to invest in compliance infrastructure and ensure that customer onboarding and reporting processes are aligned with the CBDT's expectations under the new regime.

title: Decoding PhonePe FY26: The Rs 364 Cr loss behind the Rs 2,792 Cr headline
summary:
Walmart-backed fintech PhonePe reported modest growth in FY26, but its reported loss of Rs 2,792 crore doesn't tell the complete story. A closer look at the company's financial statements shows that a significant part of the loss came from non-cash accounting adjustments instead of its core ops.
Let's first look at where PhonePe's revenue came from.
The company reported operating revenue of Rs 7,920 crore in FY26. The bulk of this came from payment services, including transaction processing fees from bill payments, digital gold, and travel bookings. It also earned from platform fees, subscription fees for payment devices and smart speakers, advertising income, and its financial services businesses such as insurance, lending, stock broking, and mutual fund distribution. Together, these businesses contributed Rs 7,619 crore during the year.
In addition, PhonePe received Rs 286 crore as incentives from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Interest income and other non-operating gains pushed its total income to Rs 8,388 crore in FY26.
On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost at Rs 4,386 crore. However, only Rs 1,994 crore, or around 45%, was paid as salaries. The remaining Rs 2,390 crore was booked as ESOP (employee stock option) expense.
Notably, around Rs 2,197 crore, or 91% of the ESOP expense, was a non-cash accounting charge. Since this does not involve an actual cash outflow, we have excluded it to understand the company's underlying operating performance.
Payment processing charges stood at Rs 1,907 crore during the year. Meanwhile, advertising and sales promotion expenses nearly doubled to Rs 956 crore. Including technology infrastructure, licensing fees, customer support, legal, logistics, and other administrative expenses, the company's total expenditure reached Rs 10,589 crore in FY26.
PhonePe also reported an exceptional loss of Rs 231 crore, largely due to goodwill impairment. Since this is another non-cash accounting adjustment and not related to regular operations, it has also been excluded from our adjusted loss calculation.
As a result, while PhonePe reported a net loss of Rs 2,792 crore in FY26, excluding the non-cash ESOP expense of Rs 2,197 crore and the exceptional goodwill impairment of Rs 231 crore brings the adjusted loss down to around Rs 364 crore.
The company also reported a loss of Rs 364 crore from its discontinued operations, mainly related to the closure of its hyperlocal commerce business, Pincode. Since the business generated limited revenue and has now been shut down, this move could help improve PhonePe's profitability going forward by eliminating a loss-making vertical.
Operationally, PhonePe continued to dominate India's UPI ecosystem. In June, it processed 10.48 billion UPI transactions, marking the fourth consecutive month in which it handled more than 10 billion transactions. The company accounted for 46.15% of total UPI transaction volume and 49.07% of transaction value, processing payments worth Rs 14.19 lakh crore during the month.
Earlier this year, PhonePe filed updated draft papers with SEBI for its proposed IPO, which is expected to raise around Rs 12,000 crore (approximately $1.5 billion). However, the Walmart-backed company has temporarily paused its listing plans amid geopolitical uncertainty and volatility in global financial markets.

title: WhatsApp overtakes CRED in UPI volume in June; PhonePe retains lead
summary:
WhatsApp overtook CRED in Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transaction volume in June, processing 150.48 million transactions compared with CRED's 141.78 million, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The crossover comes in the same month that CRED founder Kunal Shah stepped down from the fintech firm to take over as the global CEO of WhatsApp. Miten Sampat was named interim CEO of CRED following Shah's move.
In May, CRED had processed 157 million UPI transactions, ahead of WhatsApp's more than 150 million transactions.
Despite its lower transaction volume in June, CRED processed transactions worth Rs 55,117 crore and accounted for 1.91% of UPI transaction value. WhatsApp's transaction value stood at Rs 11,392 crore, translating to a 0.39% share.
Meanwhile, Walmart-backed digital payments platform PhonePe retained its dominance in the UPI ecosystem with 10.48 billion transactions in June, compared with 10.73 billion in May.
This was the fourth consecutive month that PhonePe processed more than 10 billion UPI transactions. The platform first crossed the 10 billion monthly transaction milestone in March 2026.

UPI recorded 22.72 billion transactions during June, compared with 23.2 billion transactions in May. The total transaction value declined to Rs 28.92 lakh crore from Rs 29.90 lakh crore in the previous month.
PhonePe accounted for 46.15% of total UPI transaction volume in June. In value terms, the platform held a 49.07% share after processing transactions worth Rs 14.19 lakh crore.
Google Pay retained the second spot with 7.41 billion transactions during June, translating to a 32.61% market share by volume. By value, its share stood at 33.44% after transactions worth Rs 9.67 lakh crore.
Paytm remained the third-largest UPI player with 1.80 billion transactions. The fintech major captured 7.92% market share by volume and 6.66% by value, with transactions worth Rs 1.93 lakh crore.
Among other players, Navi recorded 842.51 million transactions in June, up from more than 824 million in May, and captured a 3.71% share by volume. Flipkart-backed super.money processed 430.24 million transactions, while BHIM registered 223.54 million transactions during the month.
FamApp by Trio recorded 195.31 million transactions during the month, while Axis Bank's apps contributed 136.16 million transactions across customer-initiated, B2C, and B2B payments.
PhonePe and Google Pay together accounted for 78.76% of UPI transaction volume and 82.51% of transaction value during June. The two platforms continued to remain far ahead of other players in the country's UPI ecosystem.

title: Pronto widens AI camera rollout in homes with ‘Verified’ offering
summary:
Home services platform Pronto has confirmed that it is continuing and expanding the use of wearable cameras inside customers' homes through Pronto Verified, an opt in service that records service sessions and uses anonymized footage for AI training.
The confirmation comes nearly two months after Entrackr first reported in May that Pronto was piloting a Physical AI initiative involving AI enabled wearable cameras inside customers' homes to collect real world data for AI models. At the time, the company had described the initiative as a pilot on a small fraction of bookings.
Following Entrackr's report, peers Snabbit and Urban Company publicly said they were not pursuing similar initiatives involving wearable cameras inside customers' homes.
Responding to Entrackr's latest questionnaire, Pronto said the initiative has now evolved into Pronto Verified, which it described as an optional service.
"The camera is a recording device, and its only on device intelligence is encryption. But yes, we're scaling Pronto Verified."
According to the company, customers opt into Verified bookings, which create "a record of the work" for customers while allowing professionals to earn materially more. The company said professionals currently earn about double for every Verified booking.
Customers opt in, anonymized footage used for AI training
Pronto confirmed that anonymized footage captured during Verified bookings is used to train its AI models.
According to the company, customers are informed that recordings may be used for AI training before making a Verified booking. It said customers provide consent multiple times during the booking process and once again when the professional arrives.
The company also said customers can decline recording at any point and proceed with a standard Pronto booking instead.
"We use the anonymized footage for AI training and this is disclosed in our terms and conditions."
Data handling and privacy
Pronto said the wearable camera records video but does not capture audio.
According to the company, raw footage is encrypted, automatically deleted immediately after the work is completed, and is never accessed by humans. It said only an anonymized version, where faces and personally identifiable information have been blurred or removed, is retained.
Customers can review the anonymized recording within 48 hours of the session, after which the anonymized footage is used for AI training, the company said.
On concerns around children, family members, domestic staff or visitors who may appear in recordings, Pronto said customers are asked during booking to confirm they are consenting on behalf of everyone in the home. It also said the camera points down at the professional's work area, hands and forearms, and aims to capture nothing else.
Company on regulatory engagement
Asked whether the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) or any other regulator sought an explanation after the May controversy, Pronto did not directly answer the question.
Instead, the company said it has had "encouraging engagement with all stakeholders" and said much of the discussion in May stemmed from "a misunderstanding of how the program worked," particularly around customer disclosures. It added that disclosures have since been strengthened and are now explicit at multiple stages for participants.
Founder details ‘Pronto verified’
On Friday, after Entrackr sent its questionnaire, Pronto founder Anjali Sardana published a LinkedIn post outlining the company's approach to Pronto Verified.
In the post, Sardana said the company is "scaling Verified" and described it as an opt in booking where customers choose to have work recorded. She said professionals wear a camera that records only the work activity, customers pay a premium for the service, and professionals are paid about double compared with standard bookings.
She also reiterated that customers are informed that recordings may be used for AI training, consent is obtained at multiple stages, the camera does not capture audio, raw footage is deleted immediately after the session, and only anonymized data is retained for AI training.

The Mumbai based startup had earlier raised Rs 25 crore (around $3 million) in a pre Series A round co-led by Mount Judi Ventures and existing investor Capria Ventures in July 2024, with participation from Blume Founders Fund and other investors. It had also secured $2 million in a seed round in July 2022.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its technology platform, strengthen AI powered workforce management, deepen enterprise partnerships, and accelerate category expansion, Wiffy said in a press release.
Founded in 2019 by Vikram Sharma and Deepanshu Goyal, Wiffy operates a field services platform for home improvement and consumer durables brands.
The company provides installation, maintenance, warranty, and field services across more than 100 cities through an AI powered platform and a network of over 5,000 certified technicians. It partners with more than 100 brands, including IKEA, Panasonic, Godrej, Hettich, and Amazon, and says it has served more than one million homes across India.
Wiffy automates technician scheduling, deployment, and quality assurance through its proprietary AI powered SaaS platform, enabling brands to manage pre and post sales service operations.
According to the company, it has served more than one million homes across over 100 cities since inception. Wiffy also said that demand is driven directly by its enterprise and brand partners, resulting in minimal customer acquisition costs.

title: Ashneer Grover launches employer backed lending platform Fund My Staff
summary:
Ashneer Grover, former MD and co-founder of BharatPe, has launched Fund My Staff, a new fintech platform that enables employers to facilitate loans for their employees by acting as guarantors. Grover announced the launch of the platform in a LinkedIn post on Thursday.
The platform is designed for employers who want to support their workforce with access to credit, and for staff members with limited or no credit history who require financing backed by their employer's guarantee.
According to the website, employers can onboard staff, set the loan amount, review loan requests, and approve them by acting as guarantors. Once approved, the loan is disbursed to the employee, who repays it through monthly EMIs.
Employees can also initiate the process by sending a loan request to their employer. After the employer approves the request, the loan is processed and repaid in EMIs.
The platform says that it operates as a Lending Service Provider (LSP) in compliance with the Reserve Bank of India's digital lending guidelines. Loans are originated and sanctioned by RBI registered lending partners. The website currently lists Ash Grove Capital Private Limited, an RBI registered NBFC, as its lending partner.
The website also clarifies that employers do not pay the loan amount. Instead, they act as guarantors while the employee receives the funds and repays the loan over the selected tenure.
Fund My Staff has been developed by Delhi based Third Unicorn, the venture founded by Grover and Aseem Ghavri after Grover's exit from BharatPe. In 2024, the company launched ZeroPe, a fintech app focused on financing medical expenses. It had also introduced fantasy cricket platform CrickPe, which ceased operations in February last year.

title: PedalStart leads pre-seed round in extracurricular learning platform UpKraft
summary:
Extracurricular learning platform UpKraft has raised Rs 1.6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from a group of angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to accelerate AI product development, expand its presence across Bengaluru and Gurugram, strengthen its technology platform, operations, and customer experience, and build teams across product, technology, growth, sales, and tutor operations, UpKraft said in a press release.
Co-founded in July 2025 by Tejasvi Singh Kushwah, Varun Mangal, and Kritika Varandani, UpKraft is an AI-powered extracurricular learning platform that offers structured learning at home, in residential communities, and in schools through verified expert tutors.
According to the Bengaluru-based startup, it combines AI tools such as its AI Practice Companion and Progress Insights with standardized, level-based curricula to help students build skills while giving parents visibility into their progress. The company says it has developed standardized learning programs across music and other extracurricular disciplines and partnered with residential communities across Bengaluru and Gurugram.
Over the next 12 to 18 months, UpKraft plans to increase student enrollments, expand its presence across Bengaluru and Gurugram, improve learning outcomes, and strengthen teams across product and engineering, AI and data science, sales and business development, community and field marketing, customer success, and tutor onboarding and operations.
PedalStart is an operator-led startup accelerator focused on supporting early-stage startups. In addition to capital, it works with founders on growth strategy, operations, and market expansion through its network of operators and investors.

title: Farm Watt Innovations raises Rs 32.5 Cr co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter
summary:
Climate-focused agribusiness startup Farm Watt Innovations has raised Rs 32.5 crore ($3.36 million) in a funding round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its biomass supply chain, expand its biomass collection network, build additional aggregation hubs, invest in machinery and grow its workforce.
Founded in 2023 by Kumar Neelendu, Farm Watt Innovations aggregates and supplies agricultural biomass to compressed biogas (CBG) plants and other bioenergy facilities. The startup aims to address crop residue burning by converting agricultural waste into feedstock for renewable energy projects.
The company currently operates 15 biomass aggregation hubs across six states and plans to expand its presence to Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Bihar.
The startup said it plans to develop its own portfolio of CBG, bio-pellet and biochar plants as it expands its presence in India's bioenergy ecosystem.

title: Incred Finance posts Rs 438 Cr PAT on Rs 2,546 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
InCred Financial Services, the lending arm of InCred Holdings, delivered strong financial results in FY26 ahead of its proposed IPO. The company reported 36% year-on-year growth in operating revenue, while profits grew by 17% in the same period.
According to its consolidated financial statements, the Mumbai-based company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,546 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,872 crore in FY25.

Founded by Bhupinder Singh in 2017, InCred Finance operates as a diversified retail-focused NBFC, offering a range of lending products across personal loans, student loans, secured business loans, specialised MSME financing, and loans to financial institutions.
Interest income from loan disbursements accounted for 91% of its total operating revenue, which grew 38% year-on-year to Rs 2,331 crore. Income from fees and commission added Rs 213 crore, while the remaining operating income came from net gains on fair value changes in financial assets.
The firm also made Rs 20 crore from other non-operating sources, which pushed its total income to Rs 2,567 crore.
For the lending firm, finance costs accounted for 47% of InCred’s total expenditure and rose 47% year-on-year to Rs 922 crore in FY26. Its employee benefit expenses also increased 23% to Rs 416 crore.
Losses from impaired financial instruments, including loan write-offs, jumped 62% year-on-year to Rs 305 crore. Depreciation expenses, along with legal, collection, advertising, travel and other overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 43% to Rs 1,970 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,381 crore in the previous fiscal year.
With strong growth in loan disbursements, InCred Finance increased its profit by 17% to Rs 438 crore in FY26 from Rs 374 crore in the previous fiscal year. On a unit level, it spent Rs 0.8 to earn every rupee in FY26.
As of March 2026, the firm had total financial assets worth Rs 15,243 crore, which included a healthy cash and bank balance of Rs 824 crore
InCred Finance's parent, InCred Holdings, recently filed an updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with SEBI for its IPO, comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 1,250 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 9.90 crore equity shares. Existing shareholders, including KKR, MNI Ventures, Mohandas Pai Family, Moore Strategic, V'Ocean Investments, and others, will participate in the OFS.

title: Akumentis Healthcare records Rs 446 Cr revenue and Rs 77 Cr profit in FY26
summary:
Akumentis Healthcare recorded modest revenue growth over the past two fiscal years, with its operating revenue rising from Rs 398 crore in FY24 to Rs 446 crore in FY26. The company, however, remained profitable and reported moderate growth in its net profit.
Akumentis’ revenue from operations increased to Rs 446 crore in FY26 from Rs 434 crore in FY25, according to its annual standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


The Thane-based company markets a portfolio of more than 167 branded prescription products across therapeutic segments, including gynecology, cardiology, orthopedics, pediatrics, and dermatology. The sale of pharmaceutical products remained its sole source of operating revenue.
The company also recorded Rs 17.3 crore in other income, primarily from interest on deposits, taking its total income to Rs 464 crore in FY26 from Rs 449 crore in FY25.
Employee benefits remained the company's largest expense, decreasing to Rs 130 crore in FY26. The cost of materials consumed stood at Rs 115 crore, followed by advertising expenses of Rs 37 crore. Travelling expenses and legal and professional fees came in at Rs 28 crore and Rs 23 crore, respectively. Overall, the company's total expenditure declined marginally to Rs 360 crore in FY26 from Rs 362 crore in the previous fiscal.

Akumentis' profit increased to Rs 77 crore in FY26 from Rs 66 crore in FY25. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at 39.21% and 20.14%, respectively.
Note: We have excluded the exceptional expense of Rs 63 crore related to the impairment of loans while calculating the net profit to present the company's underlying financial performance.
On a unit basis, Akumentis spent Re 0.81 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As of March 2026, it held current assets worth Rs 271 crore, including Rs 199 crore in cash and bank balances.
Akumentis has raised a total of $19 million in funding to date, with Peak XV Partners as its largest external investor. Recently, AKUM Drugs, along with its subsidiary Akumentis Healthcare, received an income tax demand notice of Rs 134 crore.

title: AI insurtech startup NeuralKart raises seed funding led by Inflection Point Ventures
summary:

NeuralKart operates at the intersection of insurtech and industrial safety technology, targeting enterprise customers in India and overseas.

title: Spoiled inventory costs Blinkit nearly three times its adjusted EBITDA
summary:
Eternal's quick-commerce arm Blinkit had a strong quarter on paper. Orders grew fast, and the company made an adjusted EBITDA of Rs 102 crore. But a number hidden in the company's shareholder letter tells a different story.
Blinkit said it loses about 1.8% of its NOV (the total value of orders) to things like expired food, damaged goods, items lost while moving them, and theft. Most of this happens with fruits and vegetables, which go bad quickly.
Blinkit's NOV for the quarter was Rs 17,132 crore. If we take 1.8% of that, the loss comes to about Rs 308 crore.
To put the numbers in context, that Rs 308 crore loss is already baked into Blinkit's cost of goods sold, the company's shareholder letter confirms this loss is deducted before Gross Profit is calculated, which in turn feeds into adjusted EBITDA. So the Rs 102 crore in adjusted EBITDA isn't separate from this loss; it's what's left over after the Rs 308 crore has already been absorbed. If we strip that loss out, then Blinkit's underlying profit for the quarter would have been several times higher than what was reported.
In simple terms: inventory losses this quarter were close to three times the size of the profit that survived them.
This is happening because Blinkit changed the way it does business. Earlier, Blinkit worked like a middleman; it just helped connect sellers and buyers and took a small cut. Now, Blinkit buys the goods itself and sells them directly. This is called an "inventory-led" model.
This change makes Blinkit's revenue look much bigger; it grew 553% compared to last year, because now the full price of goods sold gets counted as revenue, not just the small commission. But it also means Blinkit now carries all the risk if goods don't sell in time or get damaged — and that risk is showing up as a meaningful drag on profit, even if it doesn't appear as a separate line item anywhere.
Notably, this 1.8% number does not appear anywhere in Blinkit's official, audited financial reports. It was only mentioned in the shareholder letter, in a casual answer to a question. There's no comparison with previous quarters, so there's no way to know if this problem is getting better or worse.
Meanwhile, Blinkit is also spending more money to build new stores. The cost of setting up one store has gone up from Rs 1 crore to Rs 2.5 crore. But the number of new stores added this quarter was only 200, which is one of its slowest quarters for store expansion.

title: Eternal reports Rs 20,211 Cr revenue and Rs 92 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
summary:
Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal (formerly Zomato) reported its financial results for the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27) on Wednesday. The Gurugram-based company posted a nearly 3.7X year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 92 crore during the period.
Eternal’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 20,211 crore in Q1 FY27 in contrast to Rs 7,167 crore in Q1 FY26, as per the firm’s consolidated financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sharp rise in revenue was driven by the growth of its inventory-led quick commerce business. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, operating revenue increased 17% from Rs 17,634 crore in Q4 FY26. Eternal operates multiple businesses, including its food delivery marketplace, B2B supplies platform Hyperpure, and quick commerce arm Blinkit.
Blinkit, the company's quick commerce arm, emerged as the largest revenue contributor, accounting for 77.5% of the total and reporting Rs 15,664 crore in Q1 FY27. Meanwhile, its food delivery business, Zomato, contributed 15.3% of the operating revenue and grew 37% year-on-year to Rs 3,100 crore from Rs 2,261 crore in Q1 FY26.
Meanwhile, its B2B supplies business, Hyperpure, saw revenue decline 55% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 1,034 crore, while the going out business, District, recorded 54% growth to Rs 318 crore. Including revenue from other segments and non operating income, Eternal's total income rose to Rs 20,586 crore in Q1 FY27.
Material costs accounted for 59% of the company's total expenses and stood at Rs 12,031 crore during the quarter. Delivery and related expenses grew 68.5% year-on-year to Rs 3,150 crore, while employee benefits expenses rose 29% to Rs 1,068 crore. Advertising expenses also increased 41% to Rs 945 crore during the period. Overall, Eternal's total expenditure rose to Rs 20,314 crore in Q1 FY27.
Segment-wise, the food delivery business reported a positive EBITDA of Rs 621 crore, up over 33% year-on-year. Meanwhile, Blinkit turned EBITDA positive with Rs 365 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 42 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26, while District reported a negative EBITDA of Rs 62 crore during the same period.
At the bottom line, Eternal's net profit jumped 3.7X year-on-year to Rs 92 crore in Q1 FY27, aided by strong topline growth and non-operating income.
Brokerage firm Kotak Institutional Equities retained its 'Buy' rating on Eternal ahead of its Q1 FY27 results, citing continued strength in the company's quick commerce business.
At the end of today’s trading session, Eternal’s share price stood at Rs 289.5, giving the foodtech platform a market capitalization of Rs 2,79,378 crore (approximately $29.4 billion).

title: Smartworks posts Rs 546 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; EBITDA grows over 37%
summary:
Managed office space provider Smartworks reported its financial results for the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27). The company posted 44% year-on-year growth in revenue during the period, while its EBITDA rose over 37% to Rs 346 crore.
Smartworks’ revenue from operations rose to Rs 546 crore in the Q1 FY27 from Rs 365 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Smartworks derives the bulk of its operating revenue from developing, designing and licensing serviced office spaces, along with fit out services and other ancillary offerings. The company also reported Rs 13.4 crore in non operating income, which took its total income to Rs 560 crore in Q1 FY27.
On a sequential basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 5% from Rs 520 crore in Q4 FY26.
On the cost side, depreciation (related to lease) was the largest expense at Rs 246 crore, followed by operating expenses, which were at  Rs 154 crore. Finance costs, employee benefits, and other overheads took Smartworks’s total expenditure to Rs 542 crore, compared to Rs 394 crore in the same quarter last year.
Coming to the bottom line, Smartworks turned profitable on a year-on-year basis with a net profit of Rs 13 crore in Q1 FY27, aided by other income.However, its EBITDA grew over 37% year on year to Rs 346 crore during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of 63.4%.
As of 12:35 PM today, Smartworks shares traded at around Rs 494 apiece, valuing the company at a market capitalization of Rs 5,634 crore ($593 million).

title: Zappfresh revenue grows 58% to Rs 74 Cr in Q1 FY27
summary:
DSM Fresh Foods, the parent company of omnichannel meat delivery and processed foods brand Zappfresh, reported a 58% year-on-year growth in its revenue from operations to around Rs 74 crore during the first quarter of FY27, according to its provisional business update filed with the stock exchanges.
Following the completion of the Meevaa Foods acquisition in the first week of July, the combined business currently operates at an approximate pro forma quarterly revenue run rate of Rs 85 crore, including Meevaa.
The company attributed the growth to retail expansion, wider omnichannel distribution and higher traction across its consumer and institutional businesses.
During the quarter, DSM Fresh Foods added over 70 enterprise customers across domestic and export markets. It also expanded its presence across e-commerce, quick commerce and modern retail channels, with Blinkit deliveries commencing in Mumbai.
Zappfresh expanded its retail footprint to nearly 200 co-branded outlets, surpassing its FY27 target of 150 outlets ahead of schedule. The company plans to accelerate its retail expansion through FY27 as it seeks to increase the contribution of its higher margin B2C business.
On the supply side, the company onboarded 10 new sourcing partners and initiated 270 acre land aggregation as part of its backward integration efforts. DSM Fresh Foods now works with more than 1,700 seafood farmers across its sourcing ecosystem. It also incorporated Varuna Aquatech Pvt Ltd to support the long term development of its aquaculture platform.
Internationally, the company expanded its distribution network across the UK, Canada and GCC markets and onboarded a distribution partner in Dubai.
DSM Fresh Foods reiterated its FY28 guidance of Rs 600 crore in revenue with an EBITDA margin of 18% to 20%, backed by retail expansion, value added products and deeper backward integration across its farm to fork platform.

title: InsuranceDekho enters cricket sponsorship with India’s Zimbabwe, Sri Lanka tours
summary:
Insurtech startup InsuranceDekho has entered cricket sponsorship for the first time, and signed a deal for India's upcoming tours of Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka.
According to the media reports, the company will be the Co-Presenting Sponsor for the broadcast of India's three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe. It has also secured the Title Sponsorship for India's Test series against Sri Lanka, which will be branded as the InsuranceDekho Cup.
While the company did not disclose the financial details of the partnership. This move marks a major step in its brand-building strategy through one of the country's most-watched sporting events.
Founded in 2017 by Ankit Agrawal and Ish Babbar, InsuranceDekho operates an online platform that allows customers to compare and buy insurance products across health, motor, life, and other categories.
The cricket sponsorship comes as the startup continues to scale its business in the competitive insurance distribution market. Over the past few years, InsuranceDekho has raised funding from investors including Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), Beams Fintech Fund, BNP Paribas Cardif, and Yogesh Mahansaria Family Office.
With this, InsuranceDekho joins a growing list of startups that have used cricket sponsorships to build their consumer brands, including CRED, Dream11, PhonePe, Groww, Upstox, Swiggy, Meesho, boAt, Zepto, Spinny, and Ather Energy. The list also includes several real money gaming platforms, whose presence on cricket broadcasts has declined following tighter advertising norms.

title: Medtech startup Bioscan Research raises $1 Mn in seed round led by Unicorn India Ventures
summary:
Mumbai-based medtech startup Bioscan Research has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by Unicorn India Ventures.
The proceeds will be used for market expansion, securing additional regulatory approvals, upgrading its products and creating new intellectual property.
Founded in 2017 by Anupam Lavania and Shilpa Malik, Bioscan Research develops non-invasive medical devices for the early detection of brain injuries. Its flagship product, CEREBO, uses near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and machine learning to detect intracranial injuries, enabling early diagnosis of traumatic brain injuries even before visible symptoms appear.
According to the company, its technology is designed to help healthcare providers identify brain injuries during the critical treatment window and improve patient outcomes.
Bioscan Research said it recorded 5x growth over the past 12 months. It aims to grow threefold over the next year by expanding its presence in India and overseas markets.
Founded in 2016, Unicorn India Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on deeptech startups across sectors including semiconductors, spacetech, AI infrastructure and medical diagnostics.

title: Bira 91 founder Ankur Jain exits after settlement with lenders; says company needs fresh capital
summary:
Ankur Jain, the founder of Bira 91 parent B9 Beverages, has stepped down from the board and his executive role after signing a settlement with lenders and investors, clearing the way for the company's restructuring and a fresh capital raise.
A letter by Jain, accessed by Entrackr, reveals that the settlement includes the withdrawal of all litigation, release of personal guarantees extended by the founder, and the promoter family's exit from the company's board and executive positions.
According to Jain, the settlement took much longer than expected as it involved nearly 30 stakeholders with "genuinely different, often competing interests."
"We have now reached that settlement. As part of it, my family and I will be stepping away from the board, and from our executive positions, with immediate effect," Jain wrote.
He added that all parties have agreed to withdraw claims and legal proceedings against each other, bringing the dispute to a close. Jain also confirmed that the personal guarantees he had provided for corporate loans over the years would be released as part of the agreement.
"It is, in every sense, a clean and full close of this chapter," he said.
Jain acknowledged that the prolonged negotiations had affected employees awaiting salaries, vendors awaiting payments, lenders seeking resolution, and shareholders looking for clarity. He described reaching an agreement among nearly 30 stakeholders as "close to a miracle."
The founder said Bira 91 now requires fresh capital, a clean balance sheet, and a new management team to lead the business into its next phase. He added that he would support a smooth transition and continue to back the brand from the sidelines.
B9 Beverages has faced severe financial stress over the past two years. The company reported a net loss of Rs 748.8 crore on operating revenue of Rs 638.5 crore in FY24. Amid cash flow constraints, delayed salary payments, and disputes with creditors, investors had sought changes in the company's management.
The company has not disclosed its financial statements for FY25 and FY26.
The settlement is expected to pave the way for an out of court restructuring, with existing investors likely to infuse fresh capital to revive the business after months of financial distress.
